claude_proposed_widenings.name: OngoingTrigger.on_area_enters_creature_space
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The spell triggers when the caster moves and the emanation drags over a creature — the area enters the creature's space, not the creature entering the area. on_creature_enters_area only captures creature-initiated entry. Same gap documented in Cloudkill and Moonbeam.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: whenever the Emanation enters a creature's space and whenever a creature enters the Emanation or ends its turn there

claude_proposed_widenings.name: OngoingOperation.maxTimesPerTurn (or dedup predicate)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The spell explicitly caps how many times a creature makes the save in one turn. Without this, the two encoded operations (on_creature_enters_area + on_creature_ends_turn_in_area) would each trigger independently, allowing two saves per turn. The same gap blocks Web's second operation.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: A creature makes this save only once per turn.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: Attachment.area.castTimeExclusionList
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The caster designates specific creatures at cast time who are completely unaffected by the emanation. No existing surface mechanism on area attachments supports cast-time creature exclusion. AnchoredFilter.creature_exemption_list is the closest art but is anchored-trigger-specific.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: When you cast this spell, you can designate creatures to be unaffected by it.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: DamageTypeRef.alignment_derived
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The damage type is not a free cast-time player choice — it is determined by the caster's alignment at cast time. This is mechanically distinct from CastTimeChoice (player freely picks from a list) and from a fixed type. A shape like { kind: 'alignment_derived', onGoodOrNeutral: DamageType, onEvil: DamageType } would express this precisely without conflating alignment-gating with player agency.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: the creature takes 3d8 Radiant damage (if you are good or neutral) or 3d8 Necrotic damage (if you are evil)
